video_title: Head Coach Jordan Ott Practice Media Availability | 10-9-26

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Update on Miles Bridges' injury status during preseason
quotes.excerpt: X-rays negative, looked like in pretty good shape, obviously it's the preseason so we'll be smart.
quotes.quote: X-rays negative, looked like in pretty good shape, obviously it's the preseason so we'll be smart, but worried about anything serious.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott provides a positive update on Miles Bridges following his injury scare. X-rays came back negative and the team plans to be smart with his workload during the preseason.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Developing rotation and confidence in Ryan Dunn and Jalen Bridges
quotes.excerpt: We need all the reps we can get right now with those two guys.
quotes.quote: We need all the reps we can get right now with those two guys. They worked incredibly hard over the summer and now you got to put it to action. Both have been bright spots at times and then times where it's like, okay, we got to speed it up. How do we speed it up as fast as possible? They both have added strength, you can see that. They both bring different superpowers to the table and we got to continue to bring them out.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says the Suns are prioritizing reps for Ryan Dunn and Jalen Bridges this preseason. The coach notes both players have added strength and are bringing different superpowers to the rotation.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Dunn and Rashier's individual development and on-court progress
quotes.excerpt: Ryan has taken some of those steps where he's more solid on the basketball right now.
quotes.quote: Ryan has taken some of those steps where he's more solid on the basketball right now. Rashier still has incredible hands, incredible length. He's got to know when he's in the middle of the floor he can't probably use it as much. Throwing him out there in the third quarter in a tough, tough, you know, kind of just threw him out there that wasn't his scheduled rotation. But these are all good reps, so we'll take all five games with those young guys and keep getting better.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on the development of Ryan Dunn and Rashier: Ryan is looking more solid on the ball while Rashier is utilizing his length. The coach is using these preseason games to get the young guys valuable experience.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Addressing turnover issues and team rotation strategy
quotes.excerpt: We've done a pretty good job of making the right play, some of it is overpassing.
quotes.quote: We've done a pretty good job of making the right play, some of it is overpassing. We get too deep into the paint, but we're trying to make the right play. So it's the balance of we'll lean into continue to do that as much as we can. Make the right plays, live with some turnovers. The last game was the offensive fouls. And then yeah, the younger guys definitely have to take care of it better. In both games wasn't good enough.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott addresses the team's turnover issues. He says the staff is willing to live with some mistakes as they prioritize making the right play, but notes the younger players need to take better care of the ball.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Developing Josh Okogie's offensive aggression and team role
quotes.excerpt: We want him to be more aggressive. We have such team guys and he's one of those.
quotes.quote: We want him to be more aggressive. We have such team guys and he's one of those guys that almost enjoy passing more than scoring. So just finding that balance. But his speed, his ability to connect offensively, both of them just continue to highlight. He's only a third-year player, he's going to continue to get better.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott wants to see more offensive aggression from Josh Okogie. The coach says Okogie often enjoys passing more than scoring and they are working on finding the right balance for the third-year player.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Okogie's defensive impact and areas for improvement
quotes.excerpt: He's a big catalyst to what we can do defensively, it's not only switch but take the ball.
quotes.quote: He's a big catalyst to what we can do defensively, it's not only switch but take the ball. He understands at his size he's going to have to protect the rim, he's going to have to defensive rebound. That's two areas where he's going to have to continue to get better. But his intelligence, his ability to move, his ability to take the ball from the other team is elite.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott calls Josh Okogie a big catalyst for the team defensively. While praising his elite intelligence and ability to take the ball, Ott notes Okogie must continue to improve at protecting the rim and defensive rebounding.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Okogie's high basketball IQ and academic background
quotes.excerpt: He's a thinker. He has such speed and he's so strong and fast.
quotes.quote: He's a thinker. He has such speed and he's so strong and fast, at times I feel like he's out there thinking the game. We got to get him just to play more. That's what we're trying to push him. But yeah, it doesn't surprise me. I think he got a second degree, I think he has two degrees hanging up in his place. So it's not surprising that he's excelled at different areas of our game so fast because he is so intelligent.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says Josh Okogie is a thinker who is sometimes too cerebral on the court. The coach is pushing him to just play more instinctively, noting that his high intelligence is a major asset.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating team depth and preseason progress
quotes.excerpt: I just think the depth is real. We have great depth, we got a little bigger.
quotes.quote: I just think the depth is real. We have great depth, we got a little bigger. Our young guys have hopefully taken a step. You can see them physically. The game is still a little fast for them, but yeah, overall it's been good. Adding Miles and Luke right away, you can see what they're going to bring to the table.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott believes the Suns' depth is real this season. He notes the team has gotten bigger and is already seeing the impact of new additions Miles and Luke during the preseason.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Coaching growth and the value of preseason games
quotes.excerpt: I think we're still learning. The summer was great learning, just knowing that we had 88 games.
quotes.quote: I think we're still learning. The summer was great learning, just knowing that we had 88 games of film and then we had a lot of the team back. So using some of that just to get better going into this season. But even the routine of getting back on game day is different. That's why these preseason games are good for me too, just getting back into the rhythm of everything.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says he is using the preseason to get back into the rhythm of game day coaching. He notes that while the team has a lot of returning players, they are still learning as they head into the new season.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Utilizing Devin Booker's experience and half-court offense
quotes.excerpt: He knows all the reads and he can help teach our group as we progress.
quotes.quote: He knows all the reads and he can help teach our group as we progress. And then playing in the middle of the floor with everyone pressuring, it just feels like it's a little easier to operate, run freer in the middle of the floor when you start to get along the sidelines. The way that everyone's so aggressive in the half-court, just takes some options away. So we'll try to keep it in the middle of the court, keep trying to build on it.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott discusses the Suns' half-court offense, noting that Devin Booker's experience is vital for teaching the group. The team is focusing on keeping the ball in the middle of the floor to create better operating space.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.excerpt: The first option is live, so we try to make that a scoring cut.
quotes.quote: The first option is live, so we try to make that a scoring cut. I think we've all seen Book do it, Mikal maybe even a couple years ago, would come off in that first option is live. When you're elite mid-range shooters, if we can get to it initially, let's do it. So that's a part of it for sure.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says the Suns are emphasizing the first option in their sets as a scoring cut. He notes that with elite mid-range shooters on the roster, they want to capitalize on those looks early.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Managing Devin Booker's three-point shooting and shot selection
quotes.excerpt: Just take the ones you can get. A lot of times in transitions when he finally has someone.
quotes.quote: Just take the ones you can get. A lot of times in transitions when he finally has someone off of his body, we know we can feel the emotion and energy of the building when that when that thing goes in. Just be aggressive and if you're open off the dribble three, if you're open off the dribble two, we got to let him be him. We encourage a lot of our guys to shoot pull-up threes, I just think it opens up the floor.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on Devin Booker's shot selection: We encourage our guys to shoot pull-up threes because it opens up the floor. Ott says he wants Booker to just be himself and stay aggressive.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Integrating new players and maintaining team system
quotes.excerpt: It's a little bit of both. It's using their experience, obviously you can watch film to see.
quotes.quote: It's a little bit of both. It's using their experience, obviously you can watch film to see where they've excelled at other places, but using their experience of, you know, when you come in the film room, is there music playing like there is here? Us in shootaround, do we do more than others? I think using that is helpful. But we are going to ask them to, we're going to ask them to tag, we're going to ask them to pressure. It's kind of a both. It's just like use the superpowers that help build your system, but all keep it within the framework of what you're trying to get done.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on integrating new players: We want to use their experience and superpowers while keeping everything within the framework of our system. It is about finding that balance.
